propositions: The overlap judge spends 16,040 input tokens across 12 calls with the query ticket's digest repeated verbatim in every user message while the system prompt remains byte-identical, making the repeated bytes ineligible for caching in the volatile user block.

Moving the invariant query digest from the per-call user message into the system prompt positions the shared bytes in the cacheable system block, where the engine already applies cache breakpoints via anthropic_cache_instructions=True.

The measured system prompt plus hoisted query digest reaches ~846 tokens against the measured 1024-token minimum cacheable prefix for claude-sonnet-4-6, falling short of the cache threshold and resulting in +936 input tokens (+5.8%) regression instead of savings.

Precision equivalence is preserved across 12 ordered pairs: all relations remain identical (unrelated or related_distinct) between the baseline and hoisted implementations, with confidence scores varying only within sampling variance.

The hoist is structured to preserve ordered-pair semantics by passing 'first' or 'second' to judge_one to indicate which side is hoisted, with the reference string substituted into the vacated slot via _digest_block helper.

Judge remains sequential (no parallelization) so the first call writes the prefix cache and remaining N-1 calls read it, avoiding the cold-start regression that would occur if multiple threads issued parallel calls before the prefix warmed.
